sections.title: Project Overview
blocks: **Company:** Noboribetsu Grand Hotel, Hokkaido, Japan
**Position:** Overseas Marketing Manager
**Project:** English Website Redesign
**Live Website:** https://www.nobogura.co.jp/en/
**Expertise:** Website Strategy, Visual Design, Content Strategy, International Marketing, Project Management

sections.title: Background
blocks: As the hotel sought to shift its customer mix from group and package tours toward independent travelers (FIT), increasing its ability to reach and attract international guests became a marketing priority.

The English website plays an important role in this strategy, serving not only as an official source of information but also as a tool to help guests research, evaluate and make direct booking decisions.
The project aimed to develop an English website better aligned with the needs, information-seeking behavior and expectations of international travelers.

sections.title: Problem Identification
blocks: A website designed for Japanese guests does not necessarily meet the needs of international travelers, even when its content has been translated into English.
International travelers may not share the same familiarity with Japanese culture, transportation systems, accommodation types, onsen etiquette and services typical of Japanese hotels.
The key issues to address were:
- Differences in cultural knowledge and understanding between domestic and international guests.
- Organizing information around the research behavior of independent travelers.
- Clearly communicating the hotel's distinctive features and experiential value.
- Providing clear information before guests make booking decisions.
- Connecting the hotel stay with experiences at the destination.

Drawing on my own experience as an international traveler who regularly plans independent trips, I recognized that information considered self-evident in Japan can be an important factor in an international guest's booking decision.
The objective, therefore, was not simply to translate content into English, but to build a website from the perspective of international travelers.

sections.title: Strategic Solution
blocks: Rather than approaching the project as a translation exercise or a purely visual redesign, I sought to develop the website as a customer-centric marketing platform.
The strategy focused on five elements:
- **Customer-Centric Content:** Develop content around the practical needs of international travelers.
- **Information Architecture:** Organize information logically so it is easy to find and understand.
- **Visual Communication:** Use imagery and layout to communicate the value of the guest experience clearly.
- **Destination Marketing:** Connect the hotel with experiences in Noboribetsu and the surrounding area.
- **Direct Booking Support:** Facilitate the journey from researching information to accessing the direct booking system.

sections.title: Visual Design
blocks: I personally designed the website layouts and selected typography, font sizes, imagery and information hierarchy to create visual consistency while making content easier for guests to absorb.
To me, a well-designed website should not only make a strong visual impression but also help guests find answers to the questions that truly matter to them.
@design-screens

sections.title: My Role & Agency Collaboration
blocks: ### My Role — Overseas Marketing Manager
I was responsible for the marketing direction, content strategy, visual design and coordination of the English website project.
My responsibilities included:
- Defining marketing objectives and analyzing international traveler needs.
- Developing the content strategy and information architecture.
- Personally creating the website design.
- Preparing content, imagery and implementation requirements.
- Coordinating with the website development agency.
- Reviewing content and design throughout implementation.
### External Agency

The agency was responsible for technical development, coding and translating the design into a functioning website, as well as making adjustments based on requirements and feedback throughout implementation.

sections.title: Challenges
blocks: The challenge was to balance the identity of a traditional Japanese onsen hotel, visual appeal and the diverse information needs of international guests, while ensuring that the marketing direction and design were consistently reflected in the agency's technical implementation.

sections.title: Selected Improvements
blocks: ### Onsen Information
Organized onsen content into distinct information categories to help international guests understand the bathing experience, operating hours, day-use bathing services and onsen etiquette.
### Accommodation Information
Provided information to help guests evaluate and select rooms, including room size, capacity, bed types, amenities and floor plans.
### Destination Content
Integrated Things to Do content into the website to introduce experiences beyond the hotel and help guests envision their trip more comprehensively.
### Transportation Information
Provided guidance on reaching the hotel by various means of transportation, particularly useful for independent travelers who do not use tour services.
### Booking Journey
Connected room and accommodation package information with the hotel's direct booking system.
@improvement-screens

sections.title: Results
blocks: The new English website has officially launched, providing an information platform for international travelers, supporting direct bookings and serving the hotel's international marketing activities.
**Live Website:** https://www.nobogura.co.jp/en/

sections.title: Introduction
blocks: I am a marketing professional in Japan's hospitality and tourism industry, combining customer insights, strategic thinking, creativity and management experience to develop marketing solutions for international markets.

sections.title: Think Like a Traveler
blocks: I love traveling and often plan my own trips. Exploring Kanto, Kansai and Hokkaido has exposed me to a wide range of experiences, from nature, onsen, cuisine and art to cultural festivals and entertainment.

When traveling, I pay particular attention to how businesses present their products, communicate information and shape the customer experience. This helps me approach marketing from the perspective of an international traveler.

sections.title: My Marketing Philosophy
blocks: **Think Like a Traveler. Act Like a Marketer.**
I believe marketing materials should not only be visually appealing but also communicate accurate information, highlight the value of a product and help customers make informed decisions.
I enjoy turning ideas into tangible outcomes, actively learning new skills and finding creative solutions even when resources are limited.

sections.title: Management & Leadership
blocks: My nine years of experience in Human Resources and Learning & Development within international hotel environments and Japanese companies have helped me develop capabilities in management, team development, resource planning and cross-functional collaboration.
I apply this experience to marketing projects, connecting creative ideas with business objectives through planning, coordination and execution.

sections.title: Project Background
blocks: To expand Noboribetsu Grand Hotel's brand awareness in international markets, I proactively develop partnerships with content creators, tourism promotion organizations and international travel trade partners.

sections.title: Strategic Approach
blocks: - **Creator Partnerships:** Reach international travelers through authentic experience-based content from creators.
- **Tourism Promotion:** Leverage promotional opportunities through JNTO and tourism promotion organizations.
- **Travel Trade Development:** Develop partnership opportunities with international travel agencies and tour operators.

sections.title: Project Background
blocks: In addition to promoting the products and services of Noboribetsu Grand Hotel, I focus on leveraging local tourism resources to enhance the appeal of the destination and expand the hotel's brand awareness in international markets.

sections.title: Market & Audience Insights
blocks: ### B2C — International FIT
From the perspective of an independent traveler, I recognize that international visitors may struggle to find information about lesser-known local experiences.
Providing this information helps guests plan their own trips while giving them additional reasons to choose the hotel for their stay.
### B2B — International Travel Trade

To expand brand awareness in English-speaking markets, I approach international travel companies by highlighting the commercial value of the destination, opportunities to incorporate local experiences into travel itineraries, and the potential for accommodation partnerships.

sections.title: Strategic Approach
blocks: - **Destination Research:** Research tourism resources, local experiences and seasonal activities.
- **Audience-Specific Marketing:** Develop marketing messages and materials tailored to B2C and B2B audiences.
- **Hotel Positioning:** Position the hotel as a convenient base for travelers and a potential accommodation partner for travel companies.
